conceptPanel.heading: Where software comes from
conceptPanel.text: Start software and sites from a place you trust: the Quayholt Apps portal, a bookmark, or an address you typed yourself, never an advert or a search result. If the software you need isn't in Quayholt Apps, ask the service desk; they would rather help you find it than clean up afterwards.

conceptPanel.heading: Read the address
conceptPanel.text: Read the address from the right-hand end, where the real name sits. A padlock only means nobody can listen in on the connection; it does not make a site honest, and a fake page can show one too. A familiar address is still no reason to do what a site suddenly tells you: sites get hacked.

conceptPanel.heading: The four tricks
conceptPanel.text: A web page cannot run anything on your computer by itself, so it tries to get you to: a 'verify you are human' box that wants you to paste and run something, a fake 'your browser is out of date' prompt, a full-screen alarm with a number to call, or an extension that asks to read and change everything. None of them is real. Close the page.

conceptPanel.heading: If you slipped
conceptPanel.text: If a page talked you into pasting, running, installing, calling or allowing, report it straight away: the browser Report button, the 'Report an incident' form, or the security team on extension 4444. Don't restart the computer, don't clear anything, and don't run tools from the web. If you're asked to, unplug the network cable or turn off Wi-Fi and leave the machine on.

conceptPanel.heading: The one rule
conceptPanel.text: Start from a place you trust. Never let a web page drive your computer. If in doubt, close it and report it.
